docs.title: CD Index 2 Parser
docs.text:
CD Index 2 Parser converts legacy *.IDX and *.FILE files from CD Index 2 (光碟索引大師) into modern CSV/JSON formats, preserving the full file tree structure, sizes, and modification timestamps.

This tool is for anyone who has old CD/DVD index catalogs from this popular legacy software and wants to access them with modern tools.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Parses file and directory structures from .IDX and .FILE pairs
  • Correctly decodes the 32-bit MS-DOS FAT timestamps
  • Reconstructs full file paths from tab-indented tree structures
  • Outputs clean CSV or JSON
  • Supports encodings like UTF-16, Big5, and CP950 for Traditional Chinese file names
  • Zero runtime dependencies — pure Python standard library
  • Typed API with frozen dataclasses — importable as a library

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Install from PyPI:

pip install cdindex2-parser

Parse a pair of .IDX/.FILE files into CSV:

cdindex2-parser mydisk results.csv

Or parse into JSON:

cdindex2-parser mydisk results.json --format json

Use it as a Python library:

from cdindex2_parser import parse_catalog

catalog = parse_catalog("mydisk.IDX", encoding="utf-16")
for entry in catalog:
    print(f"{entry.path}  is_dir={entry.is_dir}  size={entry.size_bytes}")

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: The public API of cdindex2-parser is documented below. All types are frozen dataclasses and all functions are pure where possible.

docs.title: parse_catalog(input_path, *, encoding='utf-16')
docs.text: Parse a .IDX/.FILE pair and return a Catalog.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: input_path : str | Path Base name or path of the IDX/FILE pair. The suffix .IDX or .FILE is recognised; otherwise .IDX is appended. encoding : str, optional Text encoding for the input files. Defaults to "utf-16" (BOM- detected). Other common encodings such as "big5" or "cp950" may be selected if the original files use a different charset.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Catalog A Catalog containing the parsed entries.

docs.title: Raises
docs.text: InputNotFoundError If either the .IDX or .FILE file does not exist. LineCountMismatchError If the two files have a different number of non-empty lines. IndentMismatchError If a data line and its corresponding name line have different indentation. MalformedRecordError If any line cannot be parsed.

docs.title: Catalog(entries) dataclass
docs.text: A collection of resolved catalog entries.

docs.title: Entry(depth, name, is_dir, size_bytes, mtime, path) dataclass
docs.text: A resolved catalog entry with full path.

docs.title: FileRecord(indent, type, size, ts, mtime) dataclass
docs.text: A single record from a .FILE line.

docs.title: NameRecord(indent, name) dataclass
docs.text: A single record from a .IDX line.

docs.title: resolve_input_path(input_path)
docs.text:
Convert a base path or suffixed path into (.IDX path, .FILE path).

The old code used input_path.rstrip('.IDX').rstrip('.FILE') which treats the argument as a character set, corrupting names like MyID.IDX → My and GAME.IDX → GAM.

This function correctly strips only the recognised suffixes and guarantees the returned pair has the same base name.

docs.title: decode_dos_datetime(ts)
docs.text: Decode a 32-bit DOS FAT timestamp into a datetime.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: ts : int 32-bit integer timestamp in MS-DOS FAT dosdate format.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: datetime datetime object; 1970-01-01T00:00:00 if the timestamp is negative or the date is invalid.

docs.title: to_csv(catalog, out)
docs.text:
Write a Catalog to CSV format.

The output uses newline="" (as recommended for csv.writer on Windows) and csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL quoting.

docs.title: to_json(catalog, out)
docs.text:
Write a Catalog to JSON format.

Output schema version 1:

.. code-block:: json

{
  "version": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "path": "dir/file.txt",
      "is_dir": false,
      "size_bytes": 226,
      "mtime": "2013-11-03T14:38:30"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text: All errors inherit from CDIndexError:

docs.text:
Bases: Exception

Base exception for all cdindex2-parser errors.

docs.text:
Bases: CDIndexError, FileNotFoundError

Raised when an input file cannot be found.

docs.text:
Bases: CDIndexError, UnicodeDecodeError

Raised when the input encoding is incorrect.

docs.title: LineCountMismatchError
docs.text:
Bases: CDIndexError, ValueError

Raised when .IDX and .FILE line counts differ.

docs.title: IndentMismatchError
docs.text:

Raised when an indentation mismatch is found.

docs.text:

Raised when a record cannot be parsed.

Initialize with an optional line number for error context.

docs.title: CD Index File Format
docs.text: The CD Index 2 software uses a pair of files with the same base name to store the index: *.IDX and *.FILE.

docs.title: *.IDX (Names & Structure)
docs.text:
This file contains the names of files and directories, with their hierarchy represented by tab indentation. Each line corresponds to one entry in the .FILE file at the same line number.

Example (shown with → representing a tab):

Root Folder
→File 1-1.txt
→File 1-2.txt
→Sub Folder 1
→→File 2-1.txt

docs.title: *.FILE (Properties)
docs.text:
This file stores properties for each corresponding line in the .IDX file. Each line follows the format [D|F]<size>.<timestamp>.

Component Meaning D Directory F File <size> Size in bytes (0 for directories) <timestamp> 32-bit MS-DOS FAT timestamp

Example (shown with → representing a tab):

D0.1334278694
→F226.1334278694
→F528.1334278694

docs.title: Encoding
docs.text:
The .IDX and .FILE files are text files encoded in a legacy codepage. Common encodings include:

  • UTF-16 (default, with or without BOM)
  • Big5 / CP950 (Traditional Chinese)
  • CP437 (US MS-DOS)

Select the encoding with the --encoding CLI option or the encoding parameter of parse_catalog().

docs.title: Timestamp Format
docs.text:
The timestamp is a 32-bit integer in the MS-DOS FAT timestamp format (dosdate). This format stores the date and time as bit fields, relative to an epoch of 1980-01-01.

The 32-bit integer is composed of two 16-bit parts:

  • Time (lower 16 bits)
  • Date (upper 16 bits)

docs.title: Decoding the Timestamp
docs.text:
Here is how the date and time components are extracted from the integer:

# ts is the 32-bit integer timestamp
dos_time = ts & 0xFFFF
dos_date = ts >> 16

# Time decoding
sec = (dos_time & 0x1F) * 2  # 5 bits for seconds (in 2-second intervals)
minute = (dos_time >> 5) & 0x3F  # 6 bits for minutes
hour = dos_time >> 11  # 5 bits for hours

# Date decoding
day = dos_date & 0x1F  # 5 bits for day
month = (dos_date >> 5) & 0xF  # 4 bits for month
year = (dos_date >> 9) + 1980  # 7 bits for year (offset from 1980)

For example, the timestamp 1130591439 is decoded as 2013-11-03 14:38:30.

docs.title: Line Correspondence
docs.text: The .IDX and .FILE files must have the same number of non-empty lines. Line n in .IDX corresponds to line n in .FILE. A mismatch raises LineCountMismatchError.

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
The easiest way to install cdindex2-parser is from the Python Package Index (PyPI):

pip install cdindex2-parser

This requires Python 3.10 or newer.

docs.title: From Source
docs.text:
You can clone the repository and install it in editable mode:

git clone https://github.com/chriskyfung/cdindex2-parser.git
cd cdindex2-parser
pip install -e .

Or install with the development extras to run tests and linting:

pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python >= 3.10
  • No runtime dependencies — pure Python standard library

docs.title: Development Extras
docs.text:
The dev extra installs tools for testing, linting, type checking, and packaging:

Extra Purpose .[dev] pytest, ruff, mypy, build, twine, pre-commit .[docs] mkdocs-material, mkdocstrings[python]

Install both:

pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

docs.title: Encoding Issues
docs.text:
If you see garbled characters for file names (especially with non-ASCII characters), the input files might be using a different encoding. The cdindex software often used big5 or cp950 for Traditional Chinese.

Solution: Use the --encoding option:

cdindex2-parser mydisk results.csv --encoding big5

Or, when using the library:

catalog = parse_catalog("mydisk.IDX", encoding="big5")

Common encodings: utf-16 (default), big5, cp950, cp437.

docs.title: Line Count Mismatch
docs.text:
You might see a LineCountMismatchError. This means the .IDX and .FILE files do not have the same number of non-empty lines, which can happen if they are corrupted or incomplete.

Solution: The parser relies on a perfect 1:1 line correspondence between the two files. You may need to manually inspect and fix the files to ensure they have the same number of lines.

docs.title: Indent Mismatch
docs.text:
You might see an IndentMismatchError. This means a .IDX line and its corresponding .FILE line have different tab indentation levels.

Solution: Check that the indentation in your .IDX file is consistent and matches the structure expected by the .FILE data.

docs.title: Malformed Record
docs.text:
You might see a MalformedRecordError. This means a line in the .IDX or .FILE file does not match the expected format ([D|F]<size>.<timestamp> for .FILE lines).

Solution: Inspect the reported line number (included in the exception) and correct the malformed line.

docs.title: Incorrect Timestamps
docs.text: If the timestamps look incorrect (e.g., a wrong year), verify you are using the latest version of the parser. The timestamp format is a 32-bit MS-DOS FAT timestamp (dosdate), not a standard Unix timestamp. The current version decodes this correctly.

docs.title: Missing File
docs.text:
You might see an InputNotFoundError. This means either the .IDX or .FILE file could not be found.

Solution: Ensure both files exist with the same base name (e.g. mydisk.IDX and mydisk.FILE), and that you passed the correct base name or path to cdindex2-parser.

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: cdindex2-parser can be used as a command-line tool or as a Python library.

docs.title: Command-Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: The cdindex2-parser command is installed automatically when you install the package.

docs.title: Basic Parsing
docs.text:
To parse a pair of .IDX/.FILE files into a CSV file, provide the base name of the input files:

cdindex2-parser mydisk results.csv

This looks for mydisk.IDX and mydisk.FILE, processes them, and writes results.csv.

You can also pass the .IDX path directly:

cdindex2-parser mydisk.IDX results.csv

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text: Option Description Default input Base name or path of the .IDX/.FILE pair (required) -o, --output Output file path <input>.csv --format Output format: csv or json Inferred from output suffix --encoding Input text encoding utf-16 --version Show version and exit —

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Parse to CSV (format inferred from .csv suffix):

cdindex2-parser mydisk results.csv

Parse to JSON:

cdindex2-parser mydisk results.json --format json

Use a non-default encoding (e.g. Big5 for Traditional Chinese names):

cdindex2-parser mydisk results.csv --encoding big5

docs.title: Output Format
docs.text:
CSV output columns:

Column Description FullPath Full path reconstructed from the indented tree IsDir 1 if directory, 0 if file SizeBytes File size in bytes (0 for directories) MtimeStr Modification time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS)

JSON output schema (version 1):

{
  "version": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "path": "Root Folder/File.txt",
      "is_dir": false,
      "size_bytes": 226,
      "mtime": "2013-11-03T14:38:30"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Python Library
docs.text:
Import and use the typed API directly:

from cdindex2_parser import parse_catalog, Catalog

# Parse an IDX/FILE pair
catalog: Catalog = parse_catalog("mydisk.IDX", encoding="utf-16")

# Iterate over entries
for entry in catalog:
    print(
        f"{entry.path}  "
        f"is_dir={entry.is_dir}  "
        f"size={entry.size_bytes}  "
        f"mtime={entry.mtime.isoformat()}"
    )

docs.title: Public API
docs.text:
Symbol Description parse_catalog(input_path, *, encoding) Parse an .IDX/.FILE pair into a Catalog Catalog Frozen dataclass holding entries (tuple of Entry) Entry A single parsed entry with path, name, is_dir, size_bytes, mtime, depth FileRecord Raw .FILE line record (indent, type, size, ts, mtime) NameRecord Raw .IDX line record (indent, name) resolve_input_path(input_path) Resolve base/suffixed path to (.IDX, .FILE) paths decode_dos_datetime(ts) Decode a 32-bit DOS FAT timestamp to datetime to_csv(catalog, out) Write a Catalog to CSV to_json(catalog, out) Write a Catalog to JSON

See the API Reference for full details.
